transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Recording: enabled (auto-transcript)
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Aisha Karim (Quantive Head of AI), Tom Brenner (Platform Lead), Ravi Shah (Security), Jen Park (Program Manager)

Summary:
Quick kickoff/check-in. Confirm network (VPC) path for private deployment, pilot scope: chat + embeddings for clinical note summarization, security posture (SOC 2 / KMS / SSO), pilot timeline and benchmarks (latency and cost targets). Agree on next steps and owners.

Topics covered:
- Pilot scope & success criteria
- Deployment mode: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC)
- Security/compliance checklist (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs)
- Data flow & retention, PHI concerns
- Benchmarks: 99th pct latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens
- Access and onboarding runbook

Action items (quick list in call): see metadata action_items for owners/dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: All right everyone thanks for joining this afternoon, we wanted to run through the activation plan and make sure the initial pilot scope is clear. Marcus, Priya and I are here from Redwood.
[00:12] Aisha Karim: Hi thanks, excited to kick this off. We really want to see a tight latency profile for clinical summarization and embeddings for search.
[00:20] Tom Brenner: One clarification, when you say "pilot" do you mean hosted or do you expect us to run private VPC? Our security folks are pushing for private, but we want to understand cost tradeoffs.
[00:34] Marcus Chen: Good question. For the pilot we can do a short hosted sandbox to move fast then switch to Dedicated or Private (VPC) for the runway—that way you can validate quality quickly. If you need strict network isolation now, we can provision a private control plane—we called it Redwood Privet in the doc, sorry "Redwood Private" — auto transcript scrambled that earlier.
[00:52] Ravi Shah: Yeah security is sticky here. SOC two reports, KMS integration and audit logs are musts. Also need to know about key custody—do you support our HSM via partner KMS?
[01:05] Marcus Chen: We support customer-managed keys through major KMS providers. HSM-backed keys are supported via integrations; I'll share the KMS integration notes. Also audit logs and token-level tracing are available in the Console.
[01:18] Aisha Karim: On the model side, we plan to use an open LLM for the first phase. We want Redwood's recommendations on quantization and perf tradeoffs.
[01:26] Marcus Chen: Absolutely. For clinical summarization the tradeoff we usually see is quantize to int8 for cost savings but keep a float16 variant for highest-quality fallback. Redwood Optimize will suggest profiles—though the transcript may say "Redwood Optimizer" sometimes.
[01:40] Jen Park: Timeline? Stakeholders want a 4-week pilot starting mid-March if possible.
[01:45] Lena Ortiz: Mid-March is tight but doable if we get access and prompts asap. Action: Jen to share stakeholders list and Slack channel so we can add the team.
[01:54] Jen Park: Will do, I can have that today.
[01:56] [Background chatter]
[02:05] Tom Brenner: For the VPC setup, do we need any particular outbound ports open? Our networking team needs a list.
[02:12] Marcus Chen: We'll provide a VPC peering / private link wiring diagram and a minimal port list. Typically it's HTTPS outbound to our control plane, and gRPC for model traffic on the private path; I'll send the diagram. Note: if you go Dedicated we can avoid egress costs via in-region routing.
[02:28] Ravi Shah: What about PHI? Will tokens or inputs be cached? Need to understand retention and delete policies.
[02:36] Priya Nair: Short answer: you can configure retention and prefix/KV caching. For PHI-heavy payloads we recommend disabling KV caching and using ephemeral sessions; we'll document the recommended settings.
[02:47] Aisha Karim: Okay that's helpful. Also, any SSO/SAML setup? We use Okta.
[02:52] Lena Ortiz: We support SAML SSO with Okta and SCIM for provisioning. Priya will coordinate SSO setup.
[02:59] Priya Nair: I'll drop the SSO runbook and a checklist.
[03:05] Marcus Chen: On benchmarks, what are the latency targets? You mentioned 99th percentile earlier—can you quantify?
[03:12] Aisha Karim: We're hoping < 300ms 99th for short-note summarization (token length ~150), and sub-100ms for small embedding calls (single vector). But we'll accept a slightly higher 99th for initial tests.
[03:25] Marcus Chen: That's ambitious but workable with Dedicated pools and tuned batching. If you prioritize latency over cost we'll recommend smaller batch windows, dedicated GPU instances, and disabling aggressive batching. If cost is priority, we use batching and KV caching—"KV cash" in the transcript sometimes—sorry, I keep seeing our auto-transcript do that.
[03:43] Tom Brenner: Good to know. On cost modeling, can you share sample unit economics? We need a model to present to finance next week.
[03:51] Lena Ortiz: Yes I'll send the pricing worksheet with examples for hosted, dedicated, and private. We'll include an estimate for int8 vs float16 variants.
[03:59] Jen Park: For pilot scale, we'll start with 3 intents (summarization, semantic search, rerank). Estimated concurrency is 20 QPS peak.
[04:09] Marcus Chen: 20 QPS peak is fine. For that load, Dedicated with autoscaling backstop should hit your latency targets; we'll propose initial pool sizes in the benchmark session.
[04:18] Ravi Shah: Can we audit model variant fallbacks? If the primary model degrades we need traceable fallback to a lower-cost/reliable model for continuity.
[04:27] Marcus Chen: Yes, the routing policy supports automatic fallback to compatible model variants and we log routing decisions in the trace. We'll demo that during the tech deep dive.
[04:36] [Interruption — line noise]
[04:44] Aisha Karim: Quick question — data residency. Some records must remain in EU. Is regional deployment possible?
[04:51] Marcus Chen: Yes, we have multi-region support; you can pin model instances to a region or route by policy. We'll include region tagging recommendations in the runbook.
[05:00] Tom Brenner: Anything from procurement/legal yet? We have contracts team that'll want standard DPA and security addenda.
[05:06] Lena Ortiz: We'll send our standard DPA and SOC two pack, also the standard enterprise addendum. Legal will prepare draft terms after the pilot commitment.
[05:15] Priya Nair: Onboarding checklist items: access provisioning, SSO, KMS confirmation, sample prompts, and benchmark window. We'll own the checklist and drive the tasks.
[05:25] Jen Park: Great. Can we get the onboarding runbook and the VPC diagram before Friday?
[05:29] Marcus Chen: Yes, I'll share a draft by Friday.
[05:33] Lena Ortiz: To recap, next steps: Lena to share pricing sheet and pilot terms; Marcus to share VPC wiring and runbook plus schedule benchmark; Priya to share SSO runbook and onboarding checklist; Jen will share stakeholder list; Ravi to share KMS details.
[05:48] Aisha Karim: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:51] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all, we'll follow up by email and update CRM with next steps.
[05:56] [Meeting ends]
